The *Avuṭṭhika Sutta* ("A Rainless Cloud", Iti 75) is a short discourse in the third section of the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.26, PTS It 64) [SuttaCentral]. The text sets forth a simile of three types of people, comparing them to different kinds of clouds: one who is like a cloud that brings no rain, one who rains only locally, and one who rains down everywhere [SuttaCentral]. The sutta is translated into numerous modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
